NAME: Cash-Runway Operating Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(ADD(cogs, xsga), xint))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap post-depreciation operating income should outperform when the firm has enough cash to cover operating and financing outflows.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This keeps the successful operating-income valuation channel but changes the liquidity conditioner from a balance-sheet scale ratio to a cash-runway concept. Profitability strengthens value when cheap operating earnings are paired with cash that can sustain the cost structure rather than merely sit on the balance sheet.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Interest-Net Operating Cushion Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(at, dlc))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating-income value should be strongest when income remains attractive after interest expense and the firm has a liquidity cushion.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Prior levered value signals often suffered when cheapness was driven by debt burden, so this charges interest directly against operating income before ranking cheapness. The cash cushion then favors firms where residual operating profitability is not exposed to near-term financing stress.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Industry-Low-Dep Cash Operating Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, ADD(at, dlc)), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(dp, at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap operating-income firms should outperform when they are liquid and have low depreciation burden relative to industry peers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The prior low-depreciation version delivered strong portfolio alpha but weak cross-sectional alignment, possibly because raw depreciation intensity mostly captured industry capital structure. Industry-adjusting depreciation burden aims to preserve the capital-consumption filter while reducing unintended sector effects.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Throughput-Backed Operating Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap operating-income firms should outperform when asset turnover is high relative to industry peers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Operating-income yield is more credible when the asset base is being used efficiently to generate sales, not merely producing a temporary accounting margin. Industry-adjusted throughput helps distinguish underpriced productive businesses from cheap firms with stagnant or underutilized assets.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Post-Dep Cash-Burn Revenue Overprice
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), ADD(sale, che))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(oiadp, at)), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should underperform when priced richly relative to sales plus cash while post-depreciation profitability is weak and cash is declining.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This refines the expensive revenue-plus-cash burn mechanism by using operating income after depreciation, which better captures whether the business can earn after capital consumption. A high signal identifies firms where valuation expectations remain elevated despite weak operating economics and deteriorating liquidity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Financing-Accelerated Cash-Burn Overprice
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), ADD(sale, che))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(oiadp, at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ACCEL(xint), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should underperform when richly valued relative to sales plus cash while operating returns are weak, interest expense is accelerating, and cash is falling.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This targets an expectations failure with both operating and financing deterioration, rather than a generic expensive-low-profitability screen. Weak post-depreciation returns become more damaging when interest costs are accelerating and the cash buffer is shrinking.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

VERDICT: flag

RATIONALE: This is essentially "Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield" with an identical second leg and interest merely subtracted from the numerator — a cosmetic tweak on a channel the archive has already probed repeatedly (After-Interest Claim Yield, Net Current Liquidity Surplus, Core Margin Floor), so it is unlikely to be informative about anything new.

---CRITIQUE Industry-Low-Dep Cash Operating Yield---
VERDICT: flag

RATIONALE: Wrapping IND_ADJ around the dp/at term of the earlier "Low-Depreciation Cash Operating Yield" is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and it is implausible that sector demeaning of one SUMRANK component explains a fmb_tstat of −1.041 coexisting with a +4.74 alpha t-stat — that disagreement points to composition/weighting or size-tilt issues, not industry effects.

---CRITIQUE Throughput-Backed Operating Yield---

RATIONALE: Conditioning cheap post-depreciation operating income on industry-adjusted asset turnover introduces a genuinely new (DuPont-efficiency) conditioner not yet in the archive and is internally consistent, though value×turnover interactions are close to well-documented profitability-value territory and the conditioner is a low-frequency, slow-moving variable.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Core-to-Net Consistent Operating Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ABS(SUB(oiadp, ni)), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap post-depreciation operating income should outperform when operating profits are not materially lost to financing, taxes, or below-the-line items.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This replaces the cosmetic interest subtraction with a core-to-bottom-line consistency test that is not another cash-cushion variant. The profitability condition strengthens operating-income value only when reported operating profits plausibly accrue to shareholders rather than being offset elsewhere in the income statement.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Depreciation-Retention Operating Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dlc))), RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ABS(oibdp), dp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap pre-depreciation operating profit should outperform when a large share of operating capacity survives depreciation charges.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This avoids another raw or industry-adjusted depreciation-intensity add-on and instead measures depreciation burden inside the operating profit stream. The interaction favors firms whose cheap cash operating earnings are not simply compensation for rapidly depreciating capital.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Multiple-Expansion Margin Deterioration
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should underperform when their sales multiple expands while operating margins deteriorate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This addresses the failed static revenue-overprice family by focusing on a mismatch in changes rather than level valuation alone. A rising valuation multiple is most vulnerable when fundamentals are moving in the opposite direction, so the signal targets expectation error rather than generic expensive-low-profitability exposure.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Refinancing-Relief Operating Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dltt), dlc))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(xint, ADD(ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), dltt), dlc)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap operating-income firms should outperform when the interest-expense drain relative to total capital claims is falling.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces the kitchen-sink cash-burn construction with a focused two-leg financing-relief mechanism. Using interest expense relative to total claims avoids the noisy gross-profit denominator and tests whether operating value becomes more attractive as financing pressure eases.
